key_headlines.title: US-Iran Ceasefire Agreement Triggers 20% Oil Price Plunge
key_headlines.summary: International oil prices fell approximately 20% following a two-week ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran, with WTI crude dropping to the $91 per barrel range. The agreement opens the Strait of Hormuz, with approximately 14 million barrels expected to arrive in South Korea this month, easing energy supply concerns.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Surges 7% on Relief Rally Following Middle East Tensions Ease
key_headlines.summary: South Korean stock markets rebounded sharply with KOSPI rising 6.87% to 5,872.34 and KOSDAQ up 5.12%, marking the first time KOSPI closed above 5,800 since March 18. The won-dollar exchange rate fell below 1,500 for the first time in 10 trading days, declining to 1,470.6 won.

key_headlines.title: Prime Minister Seeks National Support for Non-NAFTA Eco-Friendly Packaging Expansion
key_headlines.summary: Prime Minister Kim Min-seok convened an emergency economic meeting to address packaging material supply concerns affecting food supplies. The government is exploring special national support measures to accelerate the adoption of sustainable, non-NAFTA compliant packaging materials.

key_headlines.title: February Current Account Surplus Hits Record High Boosted by Semiconductor Exports
key_headlines.summary: South Korea recorded its largest-ever current account surplus in February, driven by strong semiconductor and computer peripheral exports. However, the central bank expects import increases due to rising international oil prices to be reflected from April onwards.

key_headlines.title: April Apartment Sales Forecast Plummets to Three-Year Low Amid War and Regulations
key_headlines.summary: April apartment sales forecast index fell sharply by 35.4 points to 60.9, marking the lowest level since January 2023. The decline reflects combined impact of Middle East war concerns and strengthened real estate lending regulations.

sections.Hot Economy News: The US-Iran ceasefire agreement has transformed market sentiment across Asia, with South Korea's financial markets experiencing significant relief. International crude oil prices plummeted approximately 20% to the $91 per barrel range following the two-week ceasefire agreement, easing critical energy supply concerns. South Korea expects around 14 million barrels of crude oil to arrive this month, relieving the immediate energy crisis fears for April. Prime Minister Kim Min-seok convened emergency economic meetings to address packaging material supply chain disruptions and explore government support for non-NAFTA sustainable packaging adoption. Despite ceasefire progress, government officials remain cautious about actual Hormuz Strait transit normalization and are monitoring tanker movements closely.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's February current account surplus reached a record high, primarily driven by strong semiconductor and computer peripheral exports offsetting import cost increases. The Bank of Korea expects rising international oil prices to impact import figures from April onwards, creating potential inflationary pressures. Central bank governor candidate Shin Hyun-song indicated that if Middle East tensions persist and drive inflation higher, a rate increase may be necessary in future monetary policy responses. Bond market experts increasingly expect a potential base rate increase at the April financial monetary committee meeting, citing prolonged Middle East risks and inflation pressures. Employment conditions show mixed signals with February job additions at 234,000 and unemployment at 2.9%, though youth employment remains challenged.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korea's KOSPI index surged 6.87% to close at 5,872.34, achieving its highest close above 5,800 since March 18 following the US-Iran ceasefire announcement. The KOSDAQ index rose 5.12% to 1,089.85, with both markets triggering circuit breaker halts due to sharply elevated buying demand. The won-dollar exchange rate dropped 33.6 won to close at 1,470.6, marking a return below 1,500 for the first time in 10 trading days. Non-metallic materials stocks surged over 10% while machinery and equipment sectors gained approximately 8%, reflecting market optimism about normalized energy supplies. International crude oil prices fell to below $100 per barrel intraday as relief rallies spread across Asian markets.
sections.Industry & Technology: The semiconductor industry is benefiting from AI market tailwinds while battery and chemical sectors face headwinds, according to Moody's outlook on Korean corporate polarization. SK Hynix unveiled its PQC21 SSD with 321-layer quad-level cell technology, marking the company's first high-capacity, high-performance storage solution designed for AI PC environments. The Korean Semiconductor Industry Association announced active participation in energy conservation efforts, implementing staggered work hours and flexible work arrangements in response to global energy supply uncertainties. Iron and steel industries face continued challenges despite government policy support and Chinese production cutbacks, with limited near-term outlook for business recovery. Battery industry analysts identify ESS LFP battery demand as a potential turnaround driver amid broader electric vehicle demand slowdown.
sections.Real Estate: April apartment sales forecast index plummeted 35.4 points to 60.9, the lowest level since January 2023, reflecting combined pressures from Middle East conflict uncertainties and strengthened lending regulations. Seoul's unsold apartments increased 23.85% at month-end February, particularly concentrated in urban-type residential complexes in areas like Mapo-gu. Seoul's outer-area apartment market is experiencing record-high transaction prices as renters unable to find lease properties migrate to affordable apartment sales markets. The asset threshold for top 1% real estate wealth increased by 400 million won to 3.4 billion won year-over-year, widening wealth inequality as middle-class and non-Seoul property values stagnate or decline. Real estate market polarization continues with strong demand for low-priced outer-area apartments and luxury Seoul properties while mid-range segments weaken.
sections.International Economy: The US-Iran ceasefire creates new diplomatic complexities as President Trump conditions normalization on uranium enrichment restrictions and threatens 50% tariffs on countries supplying military weapons to Iran. Trump administration officials emphasize immediate implementation of tariff policies with no exceptions or exemptions for nations violating Iran weapons sale restrictions. Southeast Asian nations are reportedly shifting sentiment toward China following concerns about Trump administration trade and diplomatic volatility, complicating ASEAN's traditional balance maintenance strategy. The ceasefire agreement, despite providing immediate market relief, reflects deep disagreements over nuclear uranium issues and ongoing negotiation uncertainties. First official peace talks between US and Iran are scheduled for Pakistan in mid-April, with global markets cautiously watching resolution prospects.
sections.AI & Economy: SK Hynix launched the PQC21 SSD with 321-layer quad-level cell technology, representing the company's first high-capacity storage solution optimized for AI PC environments and competing with offerings from major global technology firms. Meta's newly formed intelligence team has released its first AI model competing directly with offerings from OpenAI and Google, intensifying AI development race dynamics. AI data center investment continues amid infrastructure concerns as developers increasingly rely on imported machinery, electrical, and plumbing equipment with exchange rate volatility adding cost pressures. AI-driven data center construction timelines face extended schedules due to supply chain uncertainties and rising input costs from weak Korean won conditions. Long-term profitability concerns emerge among investors regarding data center project returns and exit opportunities despite near-term growth optimism.
sections.Others: Seoul Education Office distributed integrated accounting operation guidelines for kindergarten-childcare facility unification, covering comparative accounting analysis and unified budget compilation methodologies. The government stated it currently has no plans to evaluate paying transit fees to Iran for Hormuz Strait passage, despite speculation about potential toll requirements. EBS music program 'Space Psych' resumed production after three-year hiatus following funding from Google's YouTube cooperation fund, following the company's settlement on unfair bundling practices. Tax burden disparity between single and two-child households reached record levels at 3.73 percentage points, reflecting expanded government low-birth-rate support policies. GS Construction signed a memorandum of understanding with Hana Financial Group to expand advanced strategic industry investments including data center digital infrastructure development.
